options: Where an object is located compared to a reference point
How fast an object is moving
How heavy an object is
How much matter an object has
questions.explanation: Position is a location — a point. To be useful it must be given relative to a reference point, plus a distance and a direction ("6 m right of the tree").
questions.misconception: Some think position means how fast something moves; speed is about that, not the location itself.

questions.prompt: The reference point is the object sitting at 0 — but the object's true location never changed. What happens to the position number when you slide the reference point 5 m the other way?
options: It changes, because position is always measured from the reference point
It stays the same, because the object didn't move
It becomes zero
It can't be found anymore
questions.explanation: Position numbers are always measured from the reference point (0). If you move the 0-marker, every position is re-measured from the new spot, so the numbers change even though the object didn't actually move.
questions.misconception: Learners often assume position is an absolute fact like weight. It's relative — the number is meaningless without naming the 0 you measure from.

questions.prompt: Why does a good description of position usually include a direction, like "left" or "north"?
options: Because a position word like "6 m" could name two opposite spots on the line
Because direction tells you how fast to go
Because direction replaces the need for a reference point
Because you always give two numbers anyway
questions.explanation: Without a direction, "6 m" is ambiguous — there is a spot 6 m left and a spot 6 m right. Direction plus distance from a reference point names one unique location.
questions.misconception: Some learners feel a distance like 6 m is enough by itself. It isn't: distance is a size, position needs a direction to be a real location.

questions.prompt: A point is drawn on a 2D grid at (3, 2). What does the pair of numbers mean?
options: 3 units across on one axis and 2 units up on the other
3 seconds and 2 meters
3 kilograms and 2 meters
The average of 3 and 2
questions.explanation: In a coordinate pair, each number gives a distance along one axis (just like properties on a map): over 3, up 2.
questions.misconception: Learners sometimes read (3,2) as a combined value (like a sum) — but each number is independent, one per axis.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a valid description of a position?
options: The ball is 5 m to the left of the cone
The ball is fast
The ball is heavy and red
The ball is 5 m
questions.explanation: A valid position includes a reference point, a direction (left), and a distance (5 m) — "5 m to the left of the cone" is complete.
questions.misconception: The trap is "the ball is 5 m" with no direction or reference — a size, not a location.
